description: Catalog companion dashboard based on Grafana.com dashboard 25816, Linux Network Stack (node_exporter). Uses node_exporter kernel/network metrics for TCP/UDP/socket totals, conntrack and softnet health. Per-listener process/PID inventory is provided by the Kali Sentinel — Listening Sockets dashboard.

panels.description: node_nf_conntrack_entries / node_nf_conntrack_entries_limit. New connections are dropped when this reaches 100%.
panels.title: Conntrack usage

panels.description: Current number of tracked connections.
panels.title: Conntrack entries

panels.description: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
panels.title: Conntrack limit

panels.description: Connections currently in ESTABLISHED or CLOSE-WAIT state (Tcp_CurrEstab).
panels.title: TCP established

panels.description: Current UDP sockets in use (node_sockstat_UDP_inuse).
panels.title: UDP sockets in use

panels.description: Packets dropped because a CPU's softnet backlog was full (net.core.netdev_max_backlog). Should be 0.
panels.title: Softnet drops /s

panels.description: Tracked connections against nf_conntrack_max.
panels.title: Conntrack entries vs limit

panels.description: insert_failed / drop: table full or clash, packet dropped. early_drop: an existing (unreplied) entry was evicted to make room. invalid: packets that could not be associated with a connection.
panels.title: Conntrack failures /s

panels.description: Connection churn. A high insert rate with a low limit fills the table quickly. search_restart grows when the hash table is too small.
panels.title: Conntrack activity /s

panels.description: Snapshot of link state plus current throughput/packet-rate/drop-rate for the selected interfaces. RX/TX bits & pps are instantaneous rates (same $__rate_interval window as the rest of the dashboard); Drops/s and Errors/s are RX+TX combined and highlighted orange once non-zero. Carrier changes = link flaps during the selected time range.
panels.title: Interface status

panels.description: Hardware/driver-reported errors (CRC, frame, ...). Should be 0.
panels.title: Errors /s

panels.description: Packets dropped by the kernel on this interface (RX: no buffers / backlog; TX: qdisc or driver).
panels.title: Drops /s

panels.description: RX FIFO overruns mean the NIC ring buffer filled before the kernel drained it.
panels.title: FIFO, frame, collisions & carrier /s

panels.description: Average across the selected CPUs. Look at softirq, irq and system for network load.
panels.title: CPU utilisation by mode (avg of selected CPUs)

panels.description: Time spent handling interrupts. softirq is where the kernel does most of its NET_RX / NET_TX work.
panels.title: softirq & hardirq time (avg of selected CPUs)

panels.description: Every selected CPU, one line each — see the legend table on the right for exact current/mean/max per CPU, sorted highest-first. A single CPU far above the rest means network RX work is concentrated on it (check RSS queues, IRQ affinity, RPS).
panels.title: softirq time by CPU (%)

panels.description: Time each CPU spends servicing hardware interrupts. Legend table lists every CPU, sorted highest-first.
panels.title: hardirq time by CPU (%)

panels.description: Packets handled by each CPU's softnet/NAPI processing (/proc/net/softnet_stat). Stacked, so the top edge is the host total; the legend table lists every CPU's own rate. Uneven bands = uneven RX distribution.
panels.title: Packets processed /s by CPU

panels.description: Drops because the per-CPU input queue exceeded net.core.netdev_max_backlog. Should be 0 for every CPU in the legend table.
panels.title: Dropped /s by CPU (softnet backlog full)

panels.description: net_rx_action ran out of budget (netdev_budget / netdev_budget_usecs) with work left. Raising the budget or spreading load across CPUs helps.
panels.title: Time squeezed /s by CPU

panels.description: Packets waiting in each CPU's softnet backlog (RPS / non-NAPI drivers). Needs a reasonably recent node_exporter — shows 'No data' on older versions.
panels.title: Backlog length by CPU (packets)

panels.description: Packets steered to this CPU by Receive Packet Steering (IPI). Needs a reasonably recent node_exporter.
panels.title: RPS packets received /s by CPU

panels.description: Packets dropped by the per-flow limit (net.core.flow_limit_cpu_bitmap) protecting the backlog from elephant flows. Needs a reasonably recent node_exporter.
panels.title: Flow limit hits /s by CPU

panels.description: Interrupts per second delivered to each CPU for IRQ lines whose device name matches the 'NIC IRQ name regex' variable (currently matches eno1/eno2's per-queue MSI-X vectors). One line per CPU; legend table lists every CPU, sorted by current rate.
panels.title: NIC hardware interrupts /s by CPU

panels.description: Current NIC interrupt rate for each CPU, busiest first — a quick visual check that RSS/IRQ affinity is spreading interrupts evenly across CPUs rather than piling onto one.
panels.title: NIC interrupts per CPU (now)

panels.description: One line per NIC queue/IRQ vector (the 'devices' label in /proc/interrupts, e.g. eno1-TxRx-0), summed across CPUs. With RSS configured 1:1 (queue N pinned to CPU N), this should closely track the per-CPU panel above.
panels.title: NIC interrupts /s by IRQ vector

panels.description: Received packets divided by NIC hardware interrupts. Low values mean little batching (interrupt coalescing/NAPI not helping much under this load); high values mean the NIC is being polled efficiently. Keep the Interface selection and the NIC IRQ regex on the same NICs for this ratio to mean anything.
panels.title: RX packets per NIC interrupt

panels.description: Shows exactly which CPU services which NIC queue right now. With RSS/IRQ affinity pinned 1:1 you should see one non-zero cell per row/column pair (a clean diagonal per NIC) — anything off that pattern means affinity has drifted or irqbalance has been reassigning queues. The '> 0' filter drops any (CPU, IRQ vector) pair that's currently at zero, so an IRQ vector with no traffic on any CPU never shows up as a column at all, and a CPU with no active vector never shows up as a row — the table only lists what's actually happening right now.
panels.title: NIC interrupt matrix: CPU x IRQ vector (current rate, /s)

panels.description: Retransmitted segments as a share of segments sent. Sustained >1% usually indicates loss or congestion on the path.
panels.title: TCP retransmit ratio (%)

panels.description: Accept queue full (application not calling accept() fast enough, or somaxconn/backlog too small) or SYN dropped.
panels.title: Listen queue overflows & drops /s

panels.description: Sent cookies mean the SYN queue overflowed (SYN flood or undersized tcp_max_syn_backlog).
panels.title: SYN cookies /s
TCP timeouts, SYN retransmits, RSTs & bad segments /s

panels.description: Receive/send buffer errors mean the socket buffer (rmem/wmem) is too small for the packet rate or the app is too slow.
panels.title: UDP errors /s

panels.description: Many orphans can trigger 'too many orphaned sockets' (tcp_max_orphans). Large TIME_WAIT counts point to short-lived connection churn.
panels.title: TCP orphaned & TIME_WAIT sockets

panels.description: Kernel memory used by socket buffers. Compare against net.ipv4.tcp_mem / udp_mem limits.
panels.title: Socket buffer memory

list.description: Discovered from node_network_receive_bytes_total. Also drives the NIC interrupts by CPU row: node_interrupts_total's 'devices' names (e.g. eno1-TxRx-0) are matched by substring against whichever interfaces are selected here, so narrowing this to a handful of NICs shrinks both the interface panels and the interrupt panels at once -- there's no separate IRQ variable to keep in sync any more.
list.label: Interface
list.name: interface
